title: Martinelli in the 96th Minute. Brazil Break Japanese Hearts in Houston.
excerpt: Casemiro's header and a last-gasp Martinelli strike complete a dramatic comeback as Carlo Ancelotti's five-time champions survive their biggest scare yet at the 2026 World Cup.
body:
For 90 minutes, Japan had the five-time world champions exactly where they wanted them. Organised, disciplined, and increasingly confident. Then Gabriel Martinelli happened.

The Arsenal forward, introduced as a second-half substitute, squeezed a shot past goalkeeper Zion Suzuki in the sixth minute of stoppage time to send Brazil into the Round of 16 with a 2-1 victory at NRG Stadium in Houston on Monday — and send Japan home for the third consecutive World Cup with a knockout-round defeat.

"It was a mental test," Casemiro told reporters after the match, his forehead still bearing the marks of his 56th-minute equalising header. "Japan played in a very deep block, especially after scoring. Finding space against five defenders is hard. The team deserves praise mainly for the mental side, for staying calm. We knew a chance would come."

## Japan's Masterclass — and Its Cruelty

For the opening half hour, Japan absorbed Brazilian pressure with a defensive organisation that bordered on the choreographed. Vinícius Jr, the tournament's standout performer, was swarmed every time he touched the ball — two, sometimes three, defenders closing him down instantly.

Then, on 29 minutes, Brazil self-destructed. Danilo's misplaced pass in midfield was intercepted by Kaishū Sano, who surged forward, brushed past a flatfooted Casemiro, and drove a composed right-footed shot past Alisson Becker and into the bottom corner. NRG Stadium erupted — but from the blue-and-white corner.

Japan's first-half defensive masterclass was immaculate. Moriyasu's side sat deep, pressed hard when opportunities arose, and restricted Brazil to scrappy, directionless efforts. Paquetá was so anonymous he was hooked at half-time, replaced by the electric 19-year-old Endrick.

## Ancelotti's Gamble Pays Off

Carlo Ancelotti, the famously stoic Italian who was hired 14 months ago to stabilise the Brazilian programme, preached patience at the interval.

"The coach always tries to transmit calmness to us," defender Gabriel Magalhães said. "The conversations at halftime were about keeping cool heads. We know it's a long game."

The composure paid off on 56 minutes. Gabriel scooped a cross from the left that floated to the far post, where Casemiro rose brilliantly and powered a header past a helpless Suzuki. The veteran midfielder — booked early, sloppy at times — answered his critics in the most emphatic way possible.

Brazil piled on the pressure. Vinícius Jr's mazy run ended with Suzuki brilliantly pushing his shot onto the post. Endrick wasted a golden chance when he overhit a lofted pass with the goal beckoning. The clock ticked past 90, then into six minutes of added time.

It looked destined for extra time. But in the 96th minute, Bruno Guimarães received the ball on the edge of the box and slipped it through the Japanese backline. Martinelli was there, and his sharp finish found the far corner. Ancelotti leapt from his seat. The Brazilian section of the 68,000-strong crowd descended into delirium.

## Japan's Recurring Heartbreak

For Japan's Hajime Moriyasu, it was a familiar devastation. Japan had led against Sweden in the group stage before conceding a late equaliser. Against the Netherlands, they went behind twice in the second half before equalising both times. The pattern — magnificent resistance followed by late heartbreak — proved their undoing once more.

Japan have now been eliminated in the first knockout round for the third consecutive World Cup — after losing to Belgium in 2018 and Croatia in 2022 in identical fashion. It is a curse that grows heavier with each tournament.

## A Houston Spectacle — and What Comes Next

The drama unfolded at NRG Stadium, one of the World Cup's premier American venues. Houston, home to one of the largest Indian diaspora communities in the United States, has been a focal point of World Cup energy. Indian-American families have packed watch parties across the city's sprawling suburbs, and the knockout-stage intensity only amplified the atmosphere.

Brazil, who last lifted the trophy in 2002, will face the winner of Tuesday's Ivory Coast vs Norway clash in the Round of 16 on July 5 at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey — another city with a massive South Asian presence.

For NRIs across America, this World Cup is an unprecedented experience: football's grandest spectacle, quite literally on their doorstep. And on Monday evening in Houston, it delivered a finish for the ages.
